purpose: Test whether below-ground reserve/clonal state predicts future quantitative meadow stability beyond current above-ground state, without using binary reappearance as a recovery endpoint.

eligibility.sampling_frame: Census-oriented sampling of all contemporaneously baseline-Thalassia-positive stable fixed-transect nodes in Old, Middle and Lower Tampa Bay with permission for adjacent below-ground sampling.
eligibility.stratification: Do not subsample to manufacture balanced outcome classes. Attempt the full eligible baseline-Thalassia-positive core-bay frame; if permitting or field logistics require exclusions, freeze the node list and exclusion reasons before any future outcome exists.
eligibility.destructive_sampling_boundary: Cores are taken adjacent to, not directly on, permanent meter marks unless the monitoring authority explicitly permits otherwise.

recent_2023_2025_feasibility_context.boundary: Historical opened data are used only for prospective sampling feasibility. Contemporaneous baseline Thalassia presence must be rechecked before destructive sampling.

destructive_sampling_guardrail.principle: Below-ground measurement must not materially alter the permanent monitoring unit whose future state is the response.
destructive_sampling_guardrail.transect_buffer: Freeze a minimum perpendicular offset from the permanent transect line before the first core; never core on a permanent meter mark or inside the routine monitoring footprint.
destructive_sampling_guardrail.core_footprint: Freeze core diameter, depth and maximum total disturbed area per node before sampling; do not enlarge cores after inspecting TNC yield.
destructive_sampling_guardrail.restoration: Backfill/restore each core hole under the monitoring authority's protocol and record any visible disturbance at the end of sampling.
destructive_sampling_guardrail.node_specific_deviation: Any safety/access/permit exception must be documented at collection and cannot depend on future response.

primary_predictor.name: rhizome_total_nonstructural_carbohydrate
primary_predictor.unit: mg g-1 dry mass or laboratory-equivalent standardized concentration
primary_predictor.definition: predefined laboratory sum of soluble sugar + starch in rhizome tissue
primary_predictor.direction: higher reserve predicts less subsequent quantitative decline
primary_predictor.interpretation_scale: Treat rhizome TNC as a candidate longer-term reserve/buffering state, not as an acute stress-event sensor.

secondary_predictors: optional clonal/genet continuity if a validated molecular design is feasible
baseline_new_measurements.replication: At least 3 independent adjacent below-ground cores per node; process the same frozen rhizome tissue fraction in every valid core and summarize the primary predictor by node median before outcome access.

standardization.campaign_seasonality: Freeze one narrow seasonal sampling campaign before the first core. Target completion of all primary TNC sampling within 42 consecutive days.
standardization.baseline_alignment: Collect below-ground samples within 14 days before or after the node's contemporaneous fixed-transect baseline survey whenever permitted; deviations are recorded and cannot be chosen using the future response.
standardization.tissue_fraction: Before the first outcome-bearing core, freeze one living rhizome tissue definition (horizontal/vertical fraction, position relative to a living shoot, segment length, and exclusion of necrotic tissue/roots) and use it at every node.
standardization.preservation: Freeze preservation chemistry/temperature and a maximum collection-to-metabolic-arrest delay before the first core; record actual delay for every core.
standardization.assay_batch: Randomize node/core samples across assay batches with respect to bay and baseline meadow state; technical standards/controls are mandatory.
standardization.time_of_day: Record collection clock time for every core and freeze any allowable collection-time window before sampling. Do not create a time-of-day exclusion after future response access.

core_spatial_design.primary_rule: If >=3 contemporaneously Thalassia-positive meter marks exist, choose three observed marks nearest q25/q50/q75 site_m with unique anchors where possible.
core_spatial_design.two_mark_fallback: Use one anchor at each positive mark; place the third independent core at a separately frozen lateral/perpendicular offset from the midpoint-nearest positive mark.
core_spatial_design.one_mark_fallback: Place three independent non-overlapping offset cores adjacent to the single positive mark.
core_spatial_design.inference_unit: node; cores are within-node measurement replication and spatial sampling, not independent inferential units
core_spatial_design.prohibited_rescue: Do not relocate anchors after TNC assay results or future outcome access.

future_outcome.primary: next fixed-transect survey focal_frequency minus baseline focal_frequency
secondary: next survey Braun-Blanquet all-point index minus baseline
next survey blade length minus baseline where observed
next survey shoot density minus baseline where observed
future_outcome.rationale: Use continuous quantitative stability as the mechanism endpoint; annual detection transitions are not ecological recovery.

destructive_sampling_sensitivity.definition: Recalculate future focal frequency after excluding the fixed permanent meter mark(s) nearest the three TNC core anchors under one pre-frozen distance/mark rule.
destructive_sampling_sensitivity.purpose: Check that the prospective TNC association is not driven by local disturbance from destructive coring.
destructive_sampling_sensitivity.interpretation: Primary inference remains node-level full-transect frequency; a strong discrepancy is reported as a measurement-intervention concern rather than hidden.

primary_analysis.estimator: standardized coefficient of baseline rhizome TNC in a prespecified linear model for future change in focal_frequency
primary_analysis.uncertainty: Use one node-level bootstrap or permutation procedure frozen before outcome access; report a two-sided 95% interval for the standardized TNC coefficient.
primary_analysis.directional_hypothesis: higher rhizome TNC -> more positive / less negative future frequency change
primary_analysis.missing_data_rule: complete-case primary analysis; do not impute the primary below-ground predictor
primary_analysis.confirmatory_gate: Confirmatory only with at least 30 analyzable baseline-Thalassia-positive nodes and at least 8 such nodes in each core bay. Below this gate, report the prospective coefficient and uncertainty as a pilot and do not use a null result to reject rhizome-reserve buffering.
primary_analysis.support_rule: Primary support requires the frozen two-sided 95% interval for standardized_rhizome_TNC to lie above 0.

secondary_analysis.note: Secondary clonal traits and secondary biological outcomes are descriptive/supportive and cannot replace a null primary TNC -> future frequency result.
secondary_analysis.multiple_testing: Apply one declared family correction if inferential secondary tests are retained.

pre_outcome_freeze_required: q25/q50/q75 core-anchor implementation and sparse-node offset geometry
minimum perpendicular core offset from permanent transect
core diameter/depth and maximum disturbed area per node
anchor-neighborhood exclusion rule for the future disturbance sensitivity
claim_boundary: Prospective observational mechanism test; even a supported result does not by itself prove causal clonal buffering.
Do not use binary re-recording as a recovery outcome.
Do not change the primary clonal predictor after future response access.
Do not replace a null primary result with a secondary clonal trait.
If below-ground sampling is not independent of monitoring state or management intervention, document that selection explicitly.
Do not call a null TNC result decisive if fewer than 30 analyzable baseline-Thalassia-positive nodes remain or any core bay contributes fewer than 8; below that precision gate the result is a pilot.
Rhizome TNC can vary with season and recent carbon balance; sampling season, tissue fraction and preservation timing are part of the primary measurement definition, not optional metadata.
A supported TNC coefficient identifies a prospective reserve-state association, not genet identity, clonal connectivity, or causal resource translocation.
Three cores are within-node measurement replication/spatial coverage; inferential replication remains the stable transect node.

Because coring is destructive, the sampling footprint is treated as a potential intervention; any evidence that local core disturbance affected future monitoring state must be reported rather than interpreted as reserve ecology.

design_precision_gate.planning_model_terms: standardized_rhizome_TNC + baseline_frequency + baseline_Braun_Blanquet + two water-body indicators
design_precision_gate.planning_assumption: Approximate Gaussian multiple-regression benchmark, two-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power for the focal TNC term; used only to prevent an underpowered confirmatory label.
design_precision_gate.interpretation: The old 24-node design mainly detected very large partial effects. The recent frame suggests roughly 33 eligible nodes, still implying sensitivity mainly to moderate-to-large TNC effects.
